HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (SUPER DETAILED)

Consult Summary:
49-year-old woman with 6-day history of painful, foul-smelling urination, intermittent suprapubic pain, and microscopic hematuria—clinically most consistent with acute uncomplicated cystitis; empiric 3-day oral antibiotic prescribed with hydration and safety-net advice.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Dysuria (“hurts when I pee”) with malodorous urine.  
• Onset & course: Began 6 days ago; symptoms persist.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Intermittent lower-mid abdominal (suprapubic) pain, rated 7/10, non-radiating.  
  – Small “spots” of blood in urine.  
• Negatives / review of systems:  
  – No fever or chills (no thermometer at home).  
  – No flank, loin, or lower-back pain.  
  – No nausea, vomiting, change in appetite, weight loss.  
  – No urinary retention/difficulty passing urine reported.  
  – No vaginal discharge; regular menstrual periods.  
  – No prior similar urinary symptoms.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not identified.  
• IBS history: No recent change in bowel habit; no rectal bleeding.

Past Medical History:
• Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) – controlled; no recent exacerbation.  
• Denies previous kidney disease, stones, or urinary infections.  
• Surgical history: None reported.

Medications:
• Mebeverine 200 mg three times daily (dose/route/frequency as per patient).  
• Empiric antibiotic for UTI (name/dose/route/frequency not documented – prescription to be sent). *New.*

Allergies:
• Clindamycin – reaction details not stated.

Social History:
• Lives with friends.  
• Occupation: Support worker.  
• Alcohol: ~1 glass of wine per week.  
• Smoking: Never smoker.  
• Recreational drugs: Not discussed.  
• Sexual activity: Denied recent increased activity; no contributory events identified.

Family History:
• No significant familial illnesses reported.

Physical Examination:
(This was a video consultation; no vitals or physical examination performed.)

Investigations:
• None obtained; empiric treatment plan without urine dip or culture.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Suspected acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis  
  Assessment: Classic presentation (dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, microscopic hematuria, afebrile, no flank pain).  
  Plan:  
  • Prescribe 3-day course of oral antibiotic (agent/dose unspecified in transcript) – electronic Rx to Knightsbridge pharmacy.  
  • Encourage oral fluids 2.5–3 L/day.  
  • Advise cranberry juice and over-the-counter urinary alkalinising sachets.  
  • Purchase a thermometer; monitor temperature.  
  • Safety-net: seek review if pain worsens, develops fever, back/loin pain, urinary retention, or recurrent episodes.  
  • Follow-up: No routine follow-up if symptoms resolve; contact service if not improved or recurrent.

Issue 2 – Irritable bowel syndrome (historical, asymptomatic)  
  Assessment: Stable; no current bowel symptom change.  
  Plan: Continue current Mebeverine regimen.

Issue 3 – Preventive / general health  
  Plan: None specifically addressed this visit.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis – High likelihood. Acute dysuria, foul smell, suprapubic pain, hematuria, absence of systemic/flank features fit classic pattern.  
2. Urethritis (Chlamydia/Gonorrhoea) – Moderate likelihood. Dysuria ± hematuria possible; limited sexual history obtained; absence of vaginal discharge lowers probability.  
3. Distal ureteric/bladder calculi – Low-moderate likelihood. Hematuria and pain possible, but no colicky flank pain or stone history.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected elements: Exact antibiotic name/dose; complete allergy reaction detail; vital signs; urinalysis/culture; detailed sexual history; medication reconciliation beyond Mebeverine.  
● Transcript vs DDx conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional brief overlaps but clinical content intact.
